headline: Sales growth holds; one-time charges erase reported profit
summary_short: J&J sales rose 5.9% y/y to $25.4B, but diluted EPS fell to $0.09 (from $2.12) on a one-time talc litigation charge and deal costs; adjusted EPS was $2.59, down 7.5% y/y.
summary_long: Operational sales grew 6.0%: Innovative Medicine +7.9% on TREMFYA, DARZALEX, CARVYKTI and others, offset by STELARA erosion (about 690 bp); MedTech +2.5% on electrophysiology and Shockwave. U.S. sales rose 9.1%, international 1.5%. Reported EPS reflects a special charge for the proposed talc resolution plus the Firefly Bio acquisition and Sail Biomedicines collaboration; those deals also weighed on adjusted EPS. J&J raised 2026 guidance: adjusted EPS $11.05-$11.15 (midpoint $11.10, up $0.06) and operational sales $100.5B-$100.9B.
confidence_notes: The shard's EPS of $2.59 is the company's adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS, not GAAP; GAAP diluted EPS was $0.09 per the release, so the shard EPS and the GAAP EPS here are on different bases. Free cash flow is a company estimate as of October 13, 2026, and cash flow from operations will be in later SEC filings. The release does not quantify the talc charge separately in the text read here.

drivers.explanation: Operational growth of 6.0%, with U.S. sales up 9.1% and international up 1.5%; currency had a small negative effect.
Driven by TREMFYA, DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, TECVAYLI, RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE, ERLEADA, SPRAVATO and CAPLYTA, partly offset by STELARA (about 690 bp drag).
Growth from electrophysiology products and Shockwave in Cardiovascular, contact lenses in Vision and trauma in Orthopaedics.
Reflects a one-time special charge for the proposed talc litigation resolution, the Firefly Bio acquisition and the Sail Biomedicines collaboration.
Same items as net earnings: talc resolution charge and the two M&A transactions.
Adjusted EPS also reflects the impact of the Firefly Bio and Sail Biomedicines deals; the special talc charge is excluded.
CEO Joaquin Duato cited accelerating momentum in the focused portfolio and a clearer line of sight to double-digit growth by the end of the decade.
